CZ/SK Banks

Every Czech and Slovak bank code with its BIC, taken from the ČNB and NBS registries, so an IBAN fills in its bank by itself.

What it does

Adds the banks of the two official bank-code registries as Banks (Contacts → Configuration → Banks):

  • Czech Republic — Česká národní banka, Číselník kódů bank;
  • Slovakia — Národná banka Slovenska, Prevodník identifikačných kódov pre tuzemský platobný styk.

Each bank carries its four-digit bank code, its BIC where the registry has one, and its country. Names are written as the registry publishes them, untranslated.

Together with OCA's Bank from IBAN, which it installs, entering a Czech or Slovak IBAN on a bank account picks the bank by itself: SK05 1100 … is Tatra banka, CZ65 0800 … is Česká spořitelna.

It installs itself together with Bank from IBAN and has no settings.

Banks that change or disappear

The registries change a few times a year. A new version of this module brings the current lists, and when it is installed:

  • a bank's name, code, BIC and country follow the registry — a corrected BIC replaces a wrong one;
  • a bank whose code left the registry is archived, never deleted. Bank accounts that use it keep it; it is just no longer offered for new ones;
  • address, phone and e-mail are yours: neither registry publishes them, so they are never overwritten;
  • a bank you had already created by hand with the same code and country is taken over rather than duplicated.

If you need a bank to read differently from the registry, create your own bank record rather than editing the shipped one.

Coming from the earlier module

This module replaces Information about banks in Czech Republic and Slovakia (l10n_banks_cz_sk). Your administrator renames it in the database before upgrading; the bank accounts keep their banks, and the contact details the old module shipped are removed where you had not changed them.
